conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to smaller allocations.
Increase QQQ to 15% for more broad tech index exposure.
Buy VRT at 4% as a strong scanner long setup to add quality growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, balancing growth with risk management.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to higher allocations.
Increase QQQ to 15% for more broad tech index exposure.
Buy VRT at 6% as a strong scanner long setup, leaning into growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize monthly distributions.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to zero to reduce risk.
Sell high-beta single names (CRWD, SNOW) to reduce volatility.
Increase SPY to 20% for broad market exposure and stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad indices. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
